In this work, edge spheroidization was observed for the deformation-processed Cu-15Cr composites.
the instability of Cr fibers in cold-rolled Cu-15Cr in-situ composites is attributed to two mechanisms: edge spheroidization and grain boundary splitting.
When annealing temperature reaches 500 ℃, recrystallization of Cu matrix occurs and dislocation density declines. Cu grains grow up so that σdis and σgrain decrease.

With increasing annealing temperature, Cr fiber coarsening and edge spheroidization extended from edges to the center, and spacing between Cr fibers kept increasing and gradually changed into equiaxial grains, causing t and λ grow continuously and fiber strengthening is weakened considerably. Therefore, the tensile strength of composites decreases monotonically with annealing temperatures.

equilibrium solid solubility of Cr in Cu matrix increases significantly and those segregated Cr can solute back into Cu matrix. Meanwhile, fibers undergo the spheroidization process, and the conductivity of composites decreases due to impurity scattering resistance

High annealing temperature, e g, 800 ℃ in this work, leads to fiber spheroidization, grain boundary splitting, and fiber fracture. The microstructure changes of Cr fibers increases boundary scattering resistance significantly.

Taking into account of work hardening and fiber reinforcement, σdis and σgrain of deformed Cu-15Cr composites have relatively large values, while t and λ are small. Therefore, work hardening and fiber reinforcement can lead to large σCu-Cr.
